a: The disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs are generally among the ambiguous matters whose true meaning only Allah knows; in them is an indication of the inimitability of the Qur’an: it is composed of the very letters of which the Arabs’ language consists. The Arabs’ inability to produce its like — though they were the most eloquent of people — shows that the Qur’an is revelation from Allah. Opinions on interpreting these letters are many and varied. They comprise fourteen letters of the Arabic alphabet and form the phrase: “A wise text with a decisive secret”; a group of interpreters said they are Allah’s secret in the Qur’an.

But the trial of Samiri occurred, leading the Israelites to worship a golden calf that lowed. Aaron called them back to worship Allah instead of the calf, but they grew arrogant. When Moses returned and saw what his people had come to, he reproached Aaron severely.

Ishmael: Abraham's firstborn and the son of Lady Hagar. At Allah's command Abraham took Hagar and her son to the site of Mecca, leaving them with a little water and dates. When provisions ran out, she walked back and forth until Allah guided her to Zamzam water. Many people came to her. Then Allah commanded our master Abraham to build the Kaaba and raise the House's foundations: Ishmael brought stones while Abraham built until they completed it. Then came Allah's command to sacrifice Ishmael: Abraham saw in a dream that he slaughtered his son and told him. He replied, 'Father, do what you are commanded; Allah willing, you will find me patient.' Allah ransomed him with a great sacrifice. Ishmael was a horseman, the first to tame horses, patient and forbearing. He is said to be the first to speak clear Arabic. He kept his promises, commanded his family to pray and give zakat, and called for worshipping Allah and His oneness.

Adam: father of humanity; Allah created him with His Hand, made the angels prostrate to him, taught him the names, created his wife and settled both in Paradise. He warned them not to approach a particular tree, but Satan whispered to them and they ate from it. Allah sent them down to earth, enabled their means of living there and required them to worship Allah alone and urge people to do so. He made him His vicegerent on earth. Adam is Allah's messenger to his children and the first prophet.

Nuh was pious and truthful; Allah sent him to guide his people and warn them of the punishment of the Hereafter, but they disobeyed him and called him a liar. Despite this, he continued to call them to the upright religion, and a few people followed him, while the disbelievers persisted in their transgression. So Allah withheld the rain from them, and Nuh called them to believe so that Allah would lift the punishment from them; they believed and Allah lifted the punishment, but they returned to their disbelief. He kept calling them for nine hundred and fifty years; then Allah commanded him to build the ark and to take with him a pair of every kind; then the flood came and drowned them all.

He is the Friend of Allah; Allah chose him for His message and favoured him over many of His creation. Ibrahim lived among a people who worshipped the stars, and that did not satisfy him; he sensed by his innate nature that there is a greater God, until Allah guided him and chose him for His message. Ibrahim began calling his people to the oneness of Allah and His worship, but they denied him and tried to burn him, and Allah saved him from their hands. Allah made the prophets from the progeny of Ibrahim: Isma‘il and Ishaq were born to him. Ibrahim built the Ka‘bah together with Isma‘il.
